hypotheses.reasoning: The /search 500s originate in catalog-svc. Its S3 PutObject calls to s3.us-east-1 (search-artifacts-prod) start failing at 20:37:52 (#1231, 503 ServiceUnavailable), then return 500 InternalError (#1285, #1384) and 503 again (#1431). These are fast 5xx responses from S3, not timeouts, which points to an S3-side outage. search-api's CatalogClient.getBatch then fails with 'catalog-svc returned 500 (storage write failed)' (#1273, #1463, #1508, #1754), and web-bff returns GET /search 500 from the search-api 500s (#1226, #1302, #1402). The aws-sdk retry quota being exhausted (#1323, 46 failed attempts in 60s) shows retries piling up, which amplifies the impact but does not start it. The status-poller shows no S3 status signal, so the provider-side cause is not confirmed from our telemetry. The auth-svc identity-provider timeouts (#886, #1109) and account-svc pool saturation drive /login 503s, which is a separate chain and not the /search path. Index-worker GC (#328) and metrics-agent exporter drops are unrelated.

Alternative reading: the trigger is a small S3 write error rate, and aws-sdk retries (retry quota exhausted, #1323) plus search-api/web-bff retries amplify it into a sustained 20%+ 500 rate. Same lines as the primary hypothesis, weighted toward the amplification.

verdict.recommendedAction: Confirm the S3 us-east-1 incident with AWS status and the request IDs (F295E39, 3DCCAA1, 4654F30, 3271DCF). Mitigate on our side: stop retry amplification (cap aws-sdk retries/backoff in catalog-svc, add a circuit breaker on S3 writes), and have search-api serve from cache or degrade gracefully when catalog writes fail instead of returning 500. Separately, investigate the auth-svc to identity-provider timeouts (#886, #1109), which are causing the /login 503s and are not part of the /search incident.

hypotheses.reasoning: The /search 500s originate in catalog-svc. Its S3 PutObject calls to s3.us-east-1 (search-artifacts-prod) start failing at 20:37:52 (#1231, 503 ServiceUnavailable), then return 500 InternalError (#1285, #1384) and 503 again (#1431). These are fast 5xx responses from S3, not timeouts, which points to an S3-side outage. search-api's CatalogClient.getBatch then fails with 'catalog-svc returned 500 (storage write failed)' (#1273, #1463, #1508, #1754), and web-bff returns GET /search 500 from the search-api 500s (#1226, #1302, #1402). The aws-sdk retry quota being exhausted (#1323, 46 failed attempts in 60s) shows retries piling up, which amplifies the impact but does not start it. The status-poller shows no S3 status signal, so the provider-side cause is not confirmed from our telemetry. The auth-svc identity-provider timeouts (#886, #1109) and account-svc pool saturation drive /login 503s, which is a separate chain and not the /search path. Index-worker GC (#328) and metrics-agent exporter drops are unrelated.

Alternative reading: the trigger is a small S3 write error rate, and aws-sdk retries (retry quota exhausted, #1323) plus search-api/web-bff retries amplify it into a sustained 20%+ 500 rate. Same lines as the primary hypothesis, weighted toward the amplification.

input.recommendedAction: Confirm the S3 us-east-1 incident with AWS status and the request IDs (F295E39, 3DCCAA1, 4654F30, 3271DCF). Mitigate on our side: stop retry amplification (cap aws-sdk retries/backoff in catalog-svc, add a circuit breaker on S3 writes), and have search-api serve from cache or degrade gracefully when catalog writes fail instead of returning 500. Separately, investigate the auth-svc to identity-provider timeouts (#886, #1109), which are causing the /login 503s and are not part of the /search incident.
